recipes.name: Caramel Apple Cranberry Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 pastry for a 9-inch double crust pie

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Press 1 crust into a 9-inch pie plate; set aside remaining crust.
Pour lemon juice into a bowl large enough to fit apples; fill halfway with cold water. Peel and slice apples; add to lemon water and set aside.

Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in cornstarch and flour until forms a paste. Stir in 1/2 cup white sugar, brown sugar, 2 tablespoons water, vanilla extract, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and nutmeg; bring to a simmer. Drain apples; add to sugar mixture along with cranberries. Cook and stir 5 minutes; remove from heat and cool slightly.
Pour apple mixture into crust in the pie plate; press remaining crust on top. Combine 1 tablespoon white sugar and remaining 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; sprinkle over pie.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C); continue baking until top crust is golden brown, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Apple Cranberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: In this caramel apple cranberry pie recipe, dried cranberries join Granny Smith apples in this pie that is perfect for the fall season and Thanksgiving.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to jazz up a plain apple pie for the holiday season. This recipe uses a pre-made pie dough for convenience, but you can surely make your own! Sliced apples are cooked with butter, vanilla, cinnamon, and sugar-making a delicious caramel sauce. To add a hint more of sweet and tart, dried cranberries are mixed in! As a bonus, we show you how to make a simple lattice top crust.

review.reviewBody: This was the very first 2-crust (covered) pie I ever made (please don't laugh!), and so I forgot to vent the top... Naturally, it blew-up while baking and looked like it was mailed from Beirut when it came out of the oven! Even with my mid-oven pyrotechnics, it was absolutely delicious! I'll try again in a few weeks with my new-found respect for venting and see what happens! The flavor was just awesome, and it wasn't difficult to make the caramel portion at all. Thanks for a fab recipe!

WOW! I really enjoyed this pie. I have made at least 10 apple pie recipes from this site and my husband said it's the best pie I ever made. I skipped the lemon juice soak and just added my bare sliced apples. I also added pecans. Great! Thanks a lot!

I baked this pie last night as our "test" pie to bring to Thanksgiving dinner next week and OMG it's SOOO GOOD! In reading other reviews I prepped myself to be prepared for it to be a little overly sweet but it wasn't. Perfect to my sweetness liking! I used Craisins and Granny Smith and stuck to the recipe and the hub and I loved it!

Only 4 stars to start ‘cause it’s till in the oven, so more comments after we taste it. Thusfar, the apple mixture tastes wonderful. I was surprised that there was no salt, but followed without it and didn’t think it needed it when I sampled. Prepared the apples as per King Arthur recipe, i.e., soaked sliced apples in hot (160 F) cider (rather than adding lemon)for ten minutes. Also used fresh cranberries (1cup) rather than dried. Note to self: remember not to use the crust shield until the pie has set up; it flattens out the crimped edge while the dough is warming initially ??.s

Awesome!! This deserves a VERY HIGH FIVE! The consistency and color was beautiful. Flavor was incredible. My only substitutions: I used Gala apples, they were on special at the grocery. And 1 and1/2 Cups of frozen whole cranberries. Whirl berries in food processor with the 2Tbsp. sugar called for; not all the berries have to be chopped. Add this to the caramel mix with the apples. I love this pie.

I replaced the dried cranberries.for fresh ones but I soaked them overnight with Brandy! I am making this tonight. Will post pictures tomorrow on Thanksgiving day! I am also adding a scoop of Vanilla Bean Ice Cream!

Loved this pie, so did hubs. I had Honeycrisps on hand, so I used them (5) rather than the granny smiths. I used 1 cup of fresh cranberries, rather than the craisins. Everything else, I followed exactly. What a delicious recipe. 

I was surprised the directions did not mention to Vent the Crust -- some novice pie makers might not know how to do this.

I made this pie for dessert tonight, with a couple of changes. I decreased the amount of butter to 6 tablespoons and used 1 1/2 cups of fresh cranberries. Because I did not use dried cranberries, I did not introduce additional source of sugar to the filling, and the sweetness turned out to be just right for my taste and for my husband's. My husband and I found the pie to be excellent and it will definitely be a staple in our holiday table!

my husband had the best idea, we made the recipe to standing...but he added spiced rum, 2 tblspns worth. we simmered the mixture, and at the end he added the rum and simmered for a moment. try it, we love it.

This was a great recipe the only change I made was I used fresh cranberries instead of dry I added about a cup and I mixed a few tablespoons of sugar with the cranberries first and then added them to the apple mixture and the end result was delicious! The sourness from the cranberries and apples with the sweetness from the caramel sauce was just right! Will def make again in the future

Absolutely outstanding! I discovered I was out of dried cranberries, so used 1-1/4 c. chopped frozen cranberries. I increased the brown sugar by an extra 2 tablespoons to compensate for the extra tartness. Other than that, no changes. This recipe is a real keeper!
I've made this many times and it's always delicious! Everyone loves it and the family requests it the holidays.

Tasty pie! I used gala apples, since that’s what I had, and fresh cranberries as well. My apples were tiny, so I used about 8, but ended up making 2 pies. I didn’t adjust the sauce at all, but I think using fresh cranberries added more moisture. The pies came out delicious. A little bit different from a traditional apple pie, very rich and just a tiny bit tart too.

HOLY MOLY: My friends you have got to try this!!
 Because there is nothing better in this world than cranberries I used 1 1/2 cups of fresh. Should have stuck with just 1 cup because although it still tasted awesome, it also kind of tested like a cherry/apple pie, instead of apple/cranberry.

 Debra: Ma'am I -Highly Highly- encourage you to enter this into the county fair, but please use fresh cranberries. #nopieleftblueribbonawardwinner

So yummy! I made my own pie crust and even though I needed to make it a bit more moist, the pie was still delicious. I topped it with sea salt caramel ice cream, the perfect complement. Will definitely make it again.
I made this but I added some walnuts which I toasted in the oven first. it paired very well. I make this every year for Thanksgiving and Christmas.

My fiance made this pie and I helped but he did most of the work. We added caramel squares in the filling just before baking and used fresh frozen cranberries instead of dried cranberries which gave it a nice tart flavor mixed into the sweet apple filling. The filling was too runny before baking the pie as well as after it was baked. It needed more cornstarch than 2 tbsp, alot of pie filling recipes call for 1/4 cup of cornstarch, so we will add more cornstarch next time .... even with the runny filling, this pie was extremely delicious. Fantastic job to my fiance!!

Loved the smell it gave to the house. This was a good pie, but next time we'll use a deep dish because we had a mess from spill over. We also took others suggestion & used fresh cranberries which we will continue to do. I was thinking the "carmel" was an actual carmel type taste, but it is from the brown sugar & liquid together. A little disappointed about that, but now that I know it is no big deal. This pie is sweet but with the right amount of tartness to it. Will make again for sure.
Best pie at Thanksgiving and Cranberries add a tang. Used honey crisp apples and next time may try to cut sugar with some Stevia
